text:
Oxford County ranks 7th in Maine for project-based Section 8 assisted units in 2025
R. P. Boyer
Oxford County ranked 7th among 16 Maine counties in the 2025 project-based Section 8 assisted-unit ranking, with 364 assisted units.
That total was unchanged from 2024.
HUD-assisted housing programs generally lower rents for low-income households that meet program eligibility requirements. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households describes three broad categories of assistance: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Public housing is owned by local housing agencies, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, helps households lease homes in the private market. Project-based assistance is tied to specific privately owned properties with HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households receiving HUD rental assistance typically pay rent equal to 30% of their income after deductions, with the federal government covering the balance. Eligibility depends on HUD income limits that vary by location and household size, and applicants are usually placed on a waiting list until assistance becomes available.
